question: What accelerator multiples are typical past 100% of quota for SaaS AEs?
answer:
**1.2x–1.5x multiplier on commission rate for deals between 100–125% of quota; 1.5x–2.0x for 125%+ quota.** Most mid-market/enterprise SaaS use a two-tier accelerator: 1.25x at 110%, then 1.5x at 125%, flat or declining after 150% to cap top earner risk. Medallion Research data: 73% of SaaS companies use accelerators; top performers pull 40–50% of total sales comp from accelerator overachievement. **The Accelerator Function:** An accelerator is the *commission rate multiplier* applied to deals closed above 100% of annual quota. It serves three purposes: 1. **Motivation:** If an AE hits 100% quota = $200k OTE, another $10k sale at standard rate ($2k commission) feels flat. At 1.5x, it's $3k. This drives Q4 push-ins and "one more meeting" mentality. 2. **Retention:** Top 10% AEs can earn $350k–$450k in a strong year. Flat cap at $250k pushes them to competitors. Accelerators let your top performer outrun their OTE by 50–80% without raising everyone's base. 3. **Economic math:** Every incremental deal past plan has ~80–90% gross margin (no new CAC). Paying 1.5x commission on marginal deals (vs. 1.0x) still leaves 65–75% margin for the company. You're monetizing upside without breaking unit economics. **Standard Accelerator Shapes (SaaS AE):** **Tier 1: Linear with Two Breaks (Most Common)** | Attainment | Commission Rate | Example: $100k Plan | |---|---|---| | 0–99% | 5% | Up to $5k commission | | 100–124% | 6.25% (1.25x) | $100k–$124k deals at 1.25x | | 125%+ | 7.5% (1.5x) | $125k+ deals at 1.5x | At this structure, an AE hitting $130k (130% of plan) earns: - First $100k at 5% = $5k - $100k–$124k at 6.25% = $1.5k - $124k–$130k at 7.5% = $450 - Total: $6.95k commission (69.5% above 0% commission if they'd hit exactly $100k) **Tier 2: Single Accelerator + Cap (For Risk-Averse Companies)** | Attainment | Commission Rate | |---|---| | 0–99% | 5% | | 100%+ | 6% (1.2x, flat) | Flatter curve. Less upside. Easier to forecast. **Tier 3: Aggressive Accelerator (Hyper-Growth, Series B Focus)** | Attainment | Commission Rate | |---|---| | 0–99% | 5% | | 100–110% | 6.25% (1.25x) | | 110–125% | 8% (1.6x) | | 125%+ | 10% (2.0x) | Used by companies chasing ARR milestones ("We need $50M ARR by end of year"). Creates 50–70% OTE upside. Retention monster; comp spend risk if multiple AEs hit 150%. **Why NOT a Simple Flat Commission?** If you cap commission at $20k/year (100% quota = $20k commission, $150k quota = still $20k commission), you lose top performers. Pavilion data: 40% of AEs at companies with flat-capped commission plan to leave within 18 months. Accelerators cost you ~$30k–$50k extra in aggregate comp; turnover replacement cost is $400k per AE. Accelerators are cheap insurance. **Why NOT 2.0x+ Across All Overachievement?** Commission as % of revenue grows unbounded. Top AE earning $450k on $1M deal (45% of deal value) breaks unit economics and creates wage-spiral friction with product/ops teams. Median company puts a hard cap: no single AE commission exceeds 8–10% of deal value, regardless of accelerator tier. **The Clawback Edge:** If an AE hits 150% quota, then loses a deal (contract voided month 2, customer goes under), do you claw back the overachievement bonus? 60% of companies do. This requires: 1. Clawback policy documented at hire 2. Clear "deal contingency window" (usually 30–90 days post-close) 3. Clawback amount = (deal commission) + (portion of accelerator on that deal) Without clawback, AEs game Q4 closings by stretching deals with fragile terms. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Annual Quota $100k] --> B[Month 12 Attainment?] B -->|50%| C[Commission: $2.5k] B -->|75%| D[Commission: $3.75k] B -->|100%| E[Commission: $5k] B -->|110%| F[+Accelerator: $6.25k] B -->|125%| G[+Higher Accel: $7.5k] B -->|150%| H[+Cap Check: $8-9k] H -->|Clawback
